CLINICAL NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL EVALUATION
Patient Identifier: HBN-001
Age: 10 years, 4 months | Grade: 5th Grade | Handedness: Right
Referral Reason: Evaluation of persistent attention difficulties, executive dysfunction, and academic frustration.

CLINICAL HISTORY & OBSERVATIONS:
Patient is a 10-year-old child referred by their pediatrician due to increasing difficulty completing classroom tasks and sustaining focus. Parent reports difficulties with task initiation, losing school materials, and impulsive interruptions at home and school. Developmental milestones were achieved on time. No history of head trauma or seizures.

STANDARDIZED COGNITIVE & ACADEMIC ASSESSMENT:
Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children - Fifth Edition (WISC-V):
- Verbal Comprehension Index (VCI): 112 (77th percentile, High Average)
- Visual Spatial Index (VSI): 108 (70th percentile, Average)
- Fluid Reasoning Index (FRI): 115 (84th percentile, High Average)
- Working Memory Index (WMI): 88 (21st percentile, Below Average)
- Processing Speed Index (PSI): 82 (12th percentile, Below Average)
- Full Scale IQ (FSIQ): 102 (55th percentile, Average)

NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL & EXECUTIVE FUNCTIONING:
Conners 3rd Edition - Parent and Teacher Rating Scales:
- Inattention T-Score: Parent 76 (Very Elevated), Teacher 72 (Very Elevated)
- Hyperactivity/Impulsivity T-Score: Parent 68 (Elevated), Teacher 64 (Elevated)
- Executive Functioning Deficits: Significant impairment in working memory and cognitive flexibility.

DIAGNOSTIC FORMULATION & IMPRESSIONS:
1. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), Combined Presentation (ICD-10 F90.2).
2. Processing Speed and Working Memory Bottleneck relative to superior abstract fluid reasoning.

RECOMMENDATIONS & INTERVENTIONS:
1. School Accommodations (504 Plan / IEP): Extended time (1.5x) on standardized tests; reduced-distraction testing environment; visual organizational checklists.
2. Psychopharmacological Consultation: Recommend evaluation by pediatric psychiatrist for consideration of stimulant medication.
3. Behavioral Therapy: Executive function coaching and cognitive behavioral interventions focusing on emotional regulation and task planning.

COMPREHENSIVE PSYCHIATRIC AND EDUCATIONAL CONSULTATION
Patient Identifier: HBN-002
Age: 14 years, 1 month | Grade: 8th Grade | Referral Source: School Psychologist

CHIEF COMPLAINT & PRESENTING PROBLEMS:
Adolescent presents with social withdrawal, generalized anxiety symptoms, perfectionistic avoidance of school assignments, and sensory over-responsiveness.

CLINICAL INTAKE INTERVIEW & MENTAL STATUS:
Patient was cooperative, soft-spoken, and maintained intermittent eye contact. Affect was constricted and anxious. Speech was fluent with advanced vocabulary. Denies hallucinations, suicidal ideation, or thought disorder. Insight and judgment are age-appropriate.

STANDARDIZED ASSESSMENT MEASURES:
1. Multidimensional Anxiety Scale for Children (MASC-2):
   - Generalized Anxiety Index: T-Score 74 (Very Elevated)
   - Social Anxiety Scale: T-Score 78 (Very Elevated)
2. Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule, Second Edition (ADOS-2) Module 3:
   - Communication & Social Interaction Total: 9 (Meets Autism Spectrum threshold)
   - Stereotyped Behaviors & Restricted Interests: Notable insistence on sameness and intense interests in complex transit simulations.

DIAGNOSTIC SUMMARY:
1. Autism Spectrum Disorder, Level 1 (Requiring Support), without accompanying intellectual impairment (ICD-10 F84.0).
2. Generalized Anxiety Disorder (ICD-10 F41.1).
3. Social Anxiety Disorder (Social Phobia, ICD-10 F40.10).

THERAPEUTIC MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Outpatient Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) with exposure and response prevention for social anxiety.
2. Social communication skills group tailored for neurodivergent adolescents.
3. Classroom accommodations: Scheduled sensory breaks in a designated quiet zone; advance notice of changes in daily schedule.

PEDIATRIC DEVELOPMENTAL ASSESSMENT REPORT
Patient Identifier: HBN-003
Age: 7 years, 8 months | Grade: 2nd Grade

BACKGROUND & DEVELOPMENTAL CONTEXT:
Patient was evaluated following teacher concerns regarding reading acquisition, letter-sound correspondence, and phonetic decoding delays despite tiered reading intervention.

EVALUATION FINDINGS:
Woodcock-Johnson IV Tests of Achievement (WJ-IV ACH):
- Letter-Word Identification: Standard Score 78 (7th percentile, Well Below Average)
- Passage Comprehension: Standard Score 82 (12th percentile, Below Average)
- Word Attack (Phonological Decoding): Standard Score 74 (4th percentile, Significantly Below Average)
Comprehensive Test of Phonological Processing (CTOPP-2):
- Phonological Awareness Composite: Standard Score 76 (5th percentile)
- Rapid Symbolic Naming: Standard Score 80 (9th percentile)

DIAGNOSTIC IMPRESSION:
1. Specific Learning Disorder with Impairment in Reading (Developmental Dyslexia, ICD-10 F81.0).
2. Secondary academic anxiety related to oral reading in front of peers.

INTERVENTION PROTOCOL:
1. Structured Literacy Intervention: Daily 45-minute individualized reading instruction using Orton-Gillingham methodology.
2. Assistive Technology: Text-to-speech software for grade-level reading materials and audiobooks.
